title: Repro runbook — kv-shift with long-seq oddball
content:
Goal:
- Produce a compact, repeatable repro and investigative runbook for the intermittent long-sequence KV offset shift we saw in Canary on 2025-10-28. This is a personal scratchpad for experiments I ran and hypotheses to try next.

Observed symptom summary (production):
- Requests with a long prefix (~45k tokens across session) occasionally return stale context (model echoes older tokens or repeats), or produce an error in the server logs: "KV offset mismatch for session=%s expected=%d got=%d". Frequency ~0.3% on single-tenant Dedicated pool.
- When mismatch occurs, serving runtime logs show an attention kernel fallback from fast path -> compatibility path.

Hypothesis space (high level):
- H1: KV index rollover/overflow at high sequence lengths (wraparound at some internal bucket size).
- H2: Kernel selection logic uses sequence-length heuristics; long-tail sequences choose a kernel that miscomputes or has a different offset base.
- H3: Concurrent session compaction/eviction race corrupts session metadata (offset) at commit boundary.

Local repro environment (what I used):
- commit: a8f2d3c (runtime:kv-eviction-fix branch)
- docker image: ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:kvshift-debug-20251103
- GPU: A100-SXM4-40GB (driver 535.104), CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9.5
- python: 3.11.4, torch-cuda 2.2.1
- small cluster: 1 node (4 GPUs) single process serving with --disable-automatic-eviction (so I could simulate eviction manually)

Repro scripts and commands I ran (copy/paste):
1) baseline reproduce (single run):
$ python repro_kvshift.py --model zeno-v1 --prefix-file fixtures/long_prefix_45k.txt --seed 42 --batch 1 --device cuda:0 --log-level debug --save-trace out/trace1.json

2) fuzz-run (to try edge offsets):
$ python repro_kvshift.py --model zeno-v1 --prefix-file fixtures/long_prefix_45k_varied.txt --seed 0 --batch 2 --repeat 200 --device cuda:0 --trace-mode minimal --emit-kv-headers

3) manual eviction/compaction trigger (on the same run):
# in another shell, on same node:
$ ./admin/evict_session.py --session $(jq -r .session_id out/trace1.json) --force

Important flags I toggled while triaging:
- --kv-index-size=2^16 (default 64k buckets) vs reduced 2^15
- --kernel-selection-strictness=low/med/high (affects whether flash_attn can be chosen)
- ENABLE_KV_GC=1 / 0 (runtime env)

Notable logs / snippets (collected from out/trace*.log):
--- LOG START ---
[2025-11-03 13:42:11.924] INFO session=create id=ry8c session_len=45123
[2025-11-03 13:48:02.118] WARN attention: kernel fallback triggered kernel=flash_attn v=2 -> kernel=cuda_attn_v2 reason=seqlen-exceeds-tile
[2025-11-03 13:48:02.121] ERROR kvmgr: KV offset mismatch for session=ry8c expected=45122 got=65522
[2025-11-03 13:48:02.121] ERROR api: request_id=rx-991 dropped due to kv mismatch
--- LOG END ---

Interpretation notes: expected=45122 looks like 0-based token count; got=65522 is suspiciously close to 65536 - 14. That suggests a modulo/rollover at 2^16 (65536) in some offset bookkeeping.

What reproduced vs what didn't:
- Reproduced: with kv-index-size default (64k) + kernel-selection-strictness=low + ENABLE_KV_GC=1 under heavy repeated prefix submission -> saw kv mismatch in ~1/150 runs.
- Not reproduced: when kv-index-size lowered to 32k and kernel strictness=high (i.e., disallow fast kernel on borderline seqlen), no mismatch seen in 500 runs.

Quick experiments and outcomes (notes):
- Experiment A: Force fast kernel (flash_attn) on borderline seqlen -> mismatch frequency increased.
- Experiment B: Force compatibility kernel (cuda_attn_v2) always -> mismatch dropped to 0/300.
- Experiment C: Introduce random small prefix truncation (drop first 2 tokens occasionally) -> mismatch frequency decreased, points to sensitivity to absolute offset arithmetic.

Small trace excerpt (KV headers emitted):
SESSION ry8c { base_offset: 45122, epoch: 12, kv_index_mask: 0xffff }
On next append: append_len=6 -> new_offset calc -> observed stored_offset=65522 -> delta negative on signed arithmetic

Immediate theories to prioritize: 
- T1 (index-rollover): internal mask applied incorrectly for some code paths (mask vs modulus) leading to negative delta when converting to signed int32. The 0xffff hint in mask is consistent with 16-bit wrap.
- T2 (kernel path delta calc): fast kernel code computes offsets with a different word-size (e.g., 16-bit index used for perf) and doesn't zero-extend when interacting with KV manager.
- T3 (race during eviction): GC thread does a modulo adjustment while kernel concurrently reads offsets; timing window produces transient mismatch. Less likely given strong reduction when forcing compatibility kernel.

Planned next steps (ordered):
1) Add assertion in KV manager: on write/read, assert base_offset < 1<<30 and stored_offset == (base_offset + append_len) & mask. Log full 64-bit values to catch signed truncation.
2) Instrument kernel fast path to emit the offset data it uses for attention (before and after conversion). Use temporary ENV LOG_ATTN_OFFSETS=1.
3) Run A/B with kernel-selection-strictness toggled and collect histograms of base_offset values where mismatches occur.
4) Create a minimal C repro (unit test) that does the base_offset arithmetic using the same types as fast kernel (uint16/int16/int32) to see truncation.
5) If confirmed, patch: unify offset types to uint64 inside RPC boundary or explicitly mask with unsigned ops.

Mini TODO list (short):
- [ ] Push small runtime assertion and redeploy debug image
- [ ] Add kernel-side offset logs (Maya)
- [ ] Create unit test for modulo/truncation (Ethan)
- [ ] Correlate with traffic shape from Dedicated pool logs (ask SRE for logs around 2025-10-28)

Questions for the team (for async):
- Where else do we use 16-bit masks for KV indices? I grepped but might have missed inline asm paths.
- Is there any code that intentionally stores offsets as int32 in GPU kernels to save memory? (I think flash_attn had such an optimization historically.)
- Can SRE provide full server logs for that single tenant for 2025-10-28 ? I want timestamps +- 1 hour of a few errors seen.

Quick links and pointers (for myself):
- runtime/kv/kv_manager.cpp: lines 120-240 (offset arithmetic)
- runtime/attn/flash_attn_kernel.cu: look for index_t typedefs
- jira: RWINF-1642 (incident)
- PR to watch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789 (adds eviction telemetry)

Notes-to-self (formatting / reproducibility):
- Capture both server and kernel logs in binary trace if possible (I use --save-trace to bundle).
- When reporting, include the exact docker image and git sha.
- If we patch kernel, run long-fuzz 24h with varied prefixes to rule out other wrap sizes (e.g., 2^15).

Last experimental command snapshot (to rerun whole suite):
$ ./scripts/run_repro_suite.sh --image ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:kvshift-debug-20251103 --commits a8f2d3c --fuzz-iter 1000 --emit-kv-headers --log-level debug --out out/experiments/20251103

Changelog for this note:
- 2025-11-03: initial triage and first fuzz runs (JK)
- 2025-11-10: follow-up A/B on kernel selection showed strong correlation (Maya)
- 2025-11-18: added planned steps and TODOs after unit test idea (Ethan)

End of scratchpad.
